sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: {S2}, you're up.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Yesterday I wrapped up the cache changes for {PROJECT}.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Today I'm pairing with {PERSON} on the rollout script.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Heads-up that our builds have doubled in length since Monday, they take over twenty minutes now.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Yeah, I noticed that too.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Okay, {S2}?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: First thing, builds have been twice as slow since Monday, more than twenty minutes each.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: I've seen that, it's painful.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Anyway, the {PROJECT} cache work is finished.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: I'll spend today on the rollout script with {PERSON}.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Still on the logging cleanup, nothing new there.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: I'm blocked on access to the production database, and the request has been open since last week.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Hmm, who approves those now?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: I think it went to IT, but I haven't heard back.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: {S2}, anything new?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Not much, the logging cleanup continues.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: The real issue is that I still don't have production database access, and I asked a week ago.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Is that sitting with IT?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Supposedly, but there's no answer yet.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: I spent most of yesterday on the alert from the weekend.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: It turned out the payment retries were firing twice, so {NUMBER} customers got duplicate emails.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Huh, {NUMBER}.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: The fix is merged and deployed.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Wow, glad you caught it.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Today I'm back on the search work.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: So the weekend alert was the payment retries running twice, and {NUMBER} customers received every email two times.

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Sorry, how many, {NUMBER}?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Oh no.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: A fix went out last night.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: That ate most of my day, so the search work starts today.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: Okay, {S3}, your turn.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Yesterday was mostly code review.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Today I'll keep going on the settings page.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Oh, and the {PRODUCT} release moved to {DATE_ABS}, the release manager posted it this morning.

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: For {PRODUCT}, right?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: Wait, really?

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Yeah, it's in the channel.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: Before my update, did everyone see the {PRODUCT} release got pushed to {DATE_ABS}?

sentences.speaker: S1
sentences.text: For {PRODUCT}, right?

sentences.speaker: S2
sentences.text: No, since when?

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: This morning, the release manager announced it.

sentences.speaker: S3
sentences.text: For me, it was code reviews yesterday and it's the settings page today.
